content.question_text: What is the process of forcing a conversion from one data type to another called?
Write the exact syntax to cast an object reference named `staffMember` to a `Manager` class and assign it to a new variable named `boss`.
What is the single reason why you would ever want to cast an object reference from a superclass back down to a subclass?

core_requirements: To use an object in its full capacity after its actual type has been temporarily forgotten.
For example, to call a method that is unique to the subclass.
acceptable_variations: To access subclass-specific methods/fields after the object was stored in a superclass variable or array.

content.question_text: What runtime error is generated if you "lie" to the compiler and attempt to cast an object down the inheritance chain into a subclass type that it doesn't actually belong to?
What operator should you use to defensively check whether a cast will succeed before you actually attempt it?
Will the compiler allow you to cast an object to a class that is completely outside of its inheritance hierarchy (for example, casting a `String` object to an `Employee` variable)?

core_requirements: It will generate a compile-time error because there is no chance for the cast to ever succeed.
acceptable_variations: No, the compiler will stop you.

content.question_text: What happens if you use the `instanceof` operator to test a variable that is currently `null` (e.g., `x instanceof C` where `x` is `null`)? Does it crash the program?

core_requirements: It does not generate an exception/crash.
It simply returns false, because null refers to no object at all.

content.question_text: If you find yourself constantly needing to cast superclass objects down to subclasses just to call a specific method, what does this usually indicate about your code?

core_requirements: It is an indication of a design flaw in the superclass.
It might make sense to redesign the superclass to include that method instead of constantly casting.
acceptable_variations: A bad design/design flaw in the inheritance hierarchy.

content.question_text: According to the final paragraph of the section, what is the general rule regarding the use of casts and the `instanceof` operator in object-oriented programming?

core_requirements: It is best to minimize the use of casts and the instanceof operator.
acceptable_variations: Use them as little as possible.
